title: Skids, ABS & ESC
whatItIs: A skid happens when the tyres lose grip. ABS and ESC help you keep control, but they can't change the laws of physics.
keyFacts: Skids are usually caused by harsh braking, accelerating or steering, or by going too fast for the conditions.
If the rear of the car skids to the right, steer smoothly to the right to recover.
In a skid, ease off the brake and accelerator. Braking hard makes it worse.
With ABS, brake firmly in an emergency and keep your foot down: you can still steer.
ABS may not shorten your stopping distance, especially on loose or wet surfaces.

items.title: Rear skid
items.text: Ease off the pedals and steer smoothly the same way as the skid.

items.title: ABS
items.text: Stops the wheels locking when you brake hard, so you can still steer.

items.title: ESC
items.text: Brakes single wheels to keep the car stable on bends and in swerves.

items.title: Speed still matters
items.text: No system can stop a car that is going too fast for the road.

b.label: ESC
points: Works when the car starts to slide
Helps keep it pointing the right way

onTheTest.question: The rear of your car skids to the right. What should you do?
onTheTest.why: Ease off the pedals and steer smoothly in the same direction as the skid: rear goes right, steer right.

traps: ABS isn't a reason to drive closer or faster.
With ABS, keep pressing firmly even if the pedal judders.
Braking hard in a skid makes it worse.

review.notes: ESC is not covered by the Highway Code rules cited; the ESC lines are general vehicle-handling knowledge. Confirm wording against DVSA learning material.
